candidates.change_summary: Remove the 'auth' modifier from rely so anyone can authorize an address.
Remove the assignment to wards[user] so rely emits the event but does not change authorization state.
Change wards assignment to 0 so rely revokes authorization instead of granting it.
Change require condition to check wards[msg.sender] != 1, inverting authorization logic so unauthorized callers pass.
Remove the require statement entirely so anyone can call auth-protected functions.
Remove the statement that sets wards[user] to 1, so rely no longer grants authorization.
Change the assigned value from 1 to 2, so wards[user] becomes 2 instead of 1, breaking the auth check which requires exactly 1.
Change the require condition from wards[msg.sender] == 1 to wards[msg.sender] == 0, inverting the authorization logic.
Change the require condition from wards[msg.sender] == 1 to wards[msg.sender] != 1, making any value other than 1 pass auth.
Remove the require statement from the auth modifier, allowing anyone to call rely without authorization.
Replace `wards[user] = 0;` with `wards[user] = 1;` so that deny sets the ward to 1 instead of 0.
Delete the statement `wards[user] = 0;` so that deny emits the event but does not change the wards mapping.
Replace `require(wards[msg.sender] == 1, "Auth/not-authorized");` with `require(wards[msg.sender] == 0, "Auth/not-authorized");` so that auth checks for ward == 0 instead of ward == 1.
Delete the require statement in the auth modifier so that authorization checking is removed entirely.
Replace the return value with a constant address different from the immutable asset address
Remove the assignment to latestPrice so updatePrice only updates lastPriceUpdate and emits the event.
Assign latestPrice to a constant 0 instead of the input price.
Assign latestPrice to block.timestamp instead of the input price.
Remove the require statement from the auth modifier so any caller can execute updatePrice.
Replace `lastPriceUpdate = block.timestamp;` with `lastPriceUpdate = block.timestamp + 1;`
Replace `lastPriceUpdate = block.timestamp;` with `lastPriceUpdate = 0;`
Replace `lastPriceUpdate = block.timestamp;` with `lastPriceUpdate = block.timestamp - 1;`
Delete the statement `lastPriceUpdate = block.timestamp;`
Remove the `auth` modifier from `updatePrice`
Remove the `require` statement from the `auth` modifier
Replace `require(wards[msg.sender] == 1, "Auth/not-authorized");` with `require(wards[msg.sender] == 2, "Auth/not-authorized");`
Replace `require(wards[msg.sender] == 1, "Auth/not-authorized");` with `require(wards[tx.origin] == 1, "Auth/not-authorized");`
Delete the require revert on unrecognized parameter, so file succeeds silently for any what value, preventing state change to investmentManager but still emitting File event.
Replace the condition to set investmentManager only when what is NOT 'investmentManager', so the state variable never updates on the expected key.
Remove the auth modifier so that any caller can change the investmentManager, altering who can trigger the file state change.
Change the require check to always pass, letting anyone call file and change investmentManager.
Remove the require entirely, letting anyone call auth-guarded functions like file without authorization check.
Replace the call to investmentManager.totalAssets(totalSupply(), address(this)) with a plain totalSupply() call.
Replace the totalAssets() argument totalSupply() with a constant 0.
Replace investmentManager.convertToShares call with a direct ratio calculation using latestPrice, bypassing the investment manager.
Return a constant value of 0 for convertToShares, changing the conversion logic.
Multiply assets by a constant factor 2 before passing to investmentManager.convertToShares, altering the returned shares.
Call investmentManager.convertToAssets instead of convertToShares, reversing the conversion direction.
Use address(0) as the second argument to investmentManager.convertToShares, potentially changing the liquidity pool context.
